title: Minimum-order connectedness
statement: A counterexample of minimum order is connected.

title: Proper-subgraph 2-degeneracy
statement: If every proper subgraph J of a minimum counterexample G has minimum degree at most 2, then every proper subgraph H of G is 2-degenerate.

title: Universal-root elimination ordering
statement: For every vertex r of a minimum counterexample G, the graph G-r admits a degeneracy ordering of width 2.

title: Three-core criticality
statement: A minimum counterexample is a subgraph-minimal graph of minimum degree at least 3: its 3-core is the whole graph, while every proper subgraph has empty 3-core.

title: Proper-set (2,3)-sparsity
statement: For every proper vertex set S with |S| at least 2, e_G(S) is at most 2|S|-3.

title: Global edge bound
statement: If G has a degree-3 vertex, then |E(G)| is at most 2|V(G)|-2.

title: Average-degree barrier below four
statement: Every minimum counterexample satisfying MC05 has average degree strictly less than 4.

title: Arboricity-two theorem
statement: Every minimum counterexample satisfying MC04-MC05 has arboricity at most 2.

title: Two-forest decomposition
statement: The edge set of a minimum counterexample can be partitioned into two forests.

title: Two-parent orientation
statement: A minimum counterexample admits an orientation with outdegree at most 2 and indegree at least 1 at every vertex; outgoing edges may be colored with two colors so that each monochromatic directed graph is acyclic and every vertex has at most one outgoing edge of each color.

title: Small-set edge-boundary lower bound
statement: For every proper vertex set S with 2<=|S|<=5, the number of edges leaving S is at least 6-|S|.

title: Exact degree-excess identity
statement: Let A be the degree-3 vertices and D=sum_{v:d(v)>=4}(d(v)-4). Then |A|-D = 4|V(G)|-2|E(G)|.

title: Global codegree-one theorem
statement: In a graph with no 4-cycle, any two distinct vertices have at most one common neighbor.

title: Neighborhood matching theorem
statement: In a graph with no 4-cycle, the graph induced by every open neighborhood has maximum degree at most 1.

title: Disjoint second-neighbor fans
statement: For v and distinct u,w in N(v), the sets N(u)\N[v] and N(w)\N[v] are disjoint in a C4-free graph.

title: Second-neighborhood expansion bound
statement: In a C4-free graph of minimum degree at least 3, |N_2(v)| >= sum_{u in N(v)}(d(u)-1-d_{G[N(v)]}(u)) >= 2d(v)-2e(G[N(v)]). Hence |N_2(v)|>=d(v), and if d(v) is odd then |N_2(v)|>=d(v)+1.

title: Dyadic connector exclusion at a root
statement: If G has no cycle of power-of-two length, then for every vertex v, every two distinct neighbors x,y of v, and every k>=2, G-v contains no simple x-y path of length 2^k-2.

title: Edge return-spectrum exclusion
statement: If G has no power-of-two cycle, then for every edge uv and every k>=2, G-uv contains no simple u-v path of length 2^k-1.

title: Closed-neighborhood local triangle bound
statement: In a C4-free graph, the triangles containing a fixed vertex v correspond to the matching edges of G[N(v)] and are pairwise edge-disjoint outside v; their number is at most floor(d(v)/2).

title: Four-step branch separation
statement: Let b-x-f(x) and b-y-f(y) be distinct two-edge arms with x,y in N(b). If G has no 8-cycle, then there is no simple length-4 path from f(x) to f(y) internally disjoint from {b,x,y}.

title: Cubic-neighbor source premise
statement: Every vertex of a minimum counterexample has a neighbor of degree exactly 3.

title: High-degree independence source premise
statement: Vertices of degree at least 4 form an independent set in a minimum counterexample.

title: Two-thirds cubic dominance
statement: Let A be the degree-3 vertices and B the vertices of degree at least 4. Then |A|>=2|B|.

title: High-degree mass bound
statement: Under DS01-DS02, sum_{b in B}d(b)<=2|A|; in particular |{b:d(b)>=r}|<=2|A|/r for every r>=4.

title: Exact cubic-surplus identity
statement: Let D=sum_{b in B}(d(b)-4) and S=sum_{a in A}(d_A(a)-1). Then 2(|A|-2|B|)=D+S.

title: Cubic-skeleton parity law
statement: The internal branching surplus S satisfies S congruent to |A| modulo 2.

title: Component surplus formula
statement: Let c be the number of components and beta the cyclomatic number of G[A]. Then S=|A|-2c+2beta.

title: Strict cubic dominance
statement: Every noncubic minimum-order counterexample satisfies |A|>2|B|.

title: Second ratio-branch elimination
statement: Every noncubic minimum-order counterexample satisfies |A|>=2|B|+2.

title: Nonmatching-component count bound
statement: Every connected component of G[A] other than K2 contributes at least 1 to S. Hence G[A] has at most S components that are not single matching edges.

title: Bounded cubic defect kernel
statement: All but at most 3S vertices of A lie in K2 components of G[A].

title: Ratio-surplus finite-kernel theorem
statement: If |A|=2|B|+t, then D+S=2t, total high-degree excess is at most 2t, and all but at most 6t vertices of A lie in K2 components of G[A].

title: Minimum branching surplus
statement: Every noncubic minimum-order counterexample has S>=2.

title: Equality paired-incidence representation
statement: If |A|=2|B|, then every b in B has degree 4, every a in A has d_A(a)=1, G[A] is a perfect matching, and G is obtained by subdividing every edge of a simple 4-regular graph H on B once and adding a perfect matching among the subdivision vertices.

title: Equality quotient cycle doubling
statement: Every r-cycle of the quotient H in DS11 lifts to a 2r-cycle in G.

title: Equality branch elimination
statement: A minimum-order counterexample cannot satisfy |A|=2|B|.

title: Ordinary-cubic quotient
statement: Let M={a in A:d_A(a)=1} and C={a in A:d_A(a)>=2}. Form Q on B by replacing each a in M by an edge between its two B-neighbors. Then Q is simple, d_Q(b)=d_G(b)-|N(b) intersect C|, and every r-cycle of Q lifts to a 2r-cycle in G.

title: Branching-defect concentration
statement: In every noncubic minimum-order counterexample, some b in B satisfies |N(b) intersect C|>=d_G(b)-2.

title: External branch escape
statement: For the concentrating vertex b from DS16 and every x in N(b) intersect C, x has a cubic neighbor outside N[b].

title: Distinct external branch escape
statement: Distinct x,y in N(b) intersect C cannot share an external neighbor; hence their selected escape vertices may be chosen pairwise distinct.
